entities.name: Torus mesh
entities.guidance: Build a ring torus from a periodic parameter grid with major and minor loops; use slightly offset edges to avoid z-fighting.

entities.name: Identification board
entities.guidance: Show the parameter rectangle with matching opposite-edge arrows and linked selections; mark seam copies with the same canonical ID.

entities.name: Cell ledger
entities.guidance: Display V,E,F and Euler characteristic for quads or triangles, explaining the single-vertex/two-edge/one-face minimal cell decomposition separately.

state_contract.model: Use an m by n periodic quad grid with m,n>=3, unique wrapped vertex IDs and R>r>0 torus geometry. V=m*n, E=2*m*n, F=m*n. Triangulation adds one edge and one face per quad.
state_contract.authority: Combinatorial IDs own counts and adjacency; duplicated GPU seam vertices are presentation copies, not additional topological vertices.
actions: Select a seam vertex to highlight all display copies.
Change mesh resolution within valid bounds.
Return to the original cell structure.

invariants: Every periodic mesh edge has two incident faces.
V-E+F remains zero across the declared subdivisions.
Rendering seam duplication never increases the canonical vertex count.
motion_guidance: Interpolate geometric display positions only while retaining connectivity; opening the parameter rectangle is an explanatory diagram, not a topology-preserving physical deformation.
Keep identification arrows visible when the rectangle is shown apart from the torus.
known_limits: Euler characteristic alone does not classify arbitrary spaces; this record covers the declared torus cell structure.
A sphere-to-torus morph cannot preserve topology without a singularity or surgery and is outside this recipe.
Curated recipe only; no runtime scene or rendered behavior has been verified for this record.

claims.statement: Identifying opposite sides of a square constructs a torus, and Euler characteristic is the alternating count of cells by dimension.
claims.scope: Finite cell decomposition; the displayed torus grid is an authored subdivision.

object_craft.structure: Build a ring torus from a periodic parameter grid with major and minor loops; use slightly offset edges to avoid z-fighting.
object_craft.material: Muted surface faces with high-contrast selected cells; vertex size remains a display marker and does not encode a count weight.
